label: VERIFIED
extraction: Adversarial Review (AR) false-consensus failure mode and prompt fix. On SWE-PRBench, naive AR exposes false-consensus failure mode where agents converge on agreement without sufficient evidence. Single prompt iteration adding disagreement explicitly achieves highest F1 among tested methods. AR builds on test-time refinement but makes two changes: separates reviewer and critic roles, makes disagreement explicit part of protocol rather than optional self-check. Multi-agent debate uses interaction among model instances exchanging arguments before judge/final answer (Du et al., 2024; Liang et al., 2024). MARS (Wang et al., 2025) replaces round-table debate with independent reviewers aggregated by meta-reviewer. AR takes middle position: preserves interaction but restricts communication to single channel with explicit disagreement types. Goal: not open-ended debate, but evidence-grounded pushback before main agent edits/commits. AR also tested in SKILL.md form for autonomous agents without external enforcement.
